summary: An operator path to undo a guest-order claim (TKT-223 follow-up)
description:
Filed by TKT-223, whose ACs required the ownership decision to be argued rather than assumed. It was
argued, and this is the part the argument left open.

**The problem, in ADR-049 § TKT-223's own words:** *"A claim is destructive, exclusive, permanent and
unrecoverable. The first holder to claim takes the order away from its buyer, and there is no
un-claim path — no endpoint, no CLI, no support tool. The buyer's recourse is nothing."*

The proof of ownership is the order reference alone, deliberately: matching the email would refuse a
buyer who signed up with a different address. The cost of that choice is that anyone holding a leaked
reference can permanently take an order — and references **do** leak, because the gateway logs them
via the URL path (**TKT-202**, open).

Today the only remedy is a manual `UPDATE` against the commerce database.

**Acceptance Criteria:**
- [ ] An operator can detach an order from the customer it is attributed to, restoring it to
  unattributed so the real buyer can claim it.
- [ ] The plan states **who may do this and how they are authenticated**. It is a support action on
  someone else's purchase, so "an internal endpoint" is the start of the answer and not the whole of
  it — ADR-043 decides the guard, and the back office already has a staff credential and a role
  matrix (ADR-042/TKT-197).
- [ ] The action is **recorded**, with who did it and why. An un-claim that leaves no trace turns a
  support tool into a way to move purchases quietly.
- [ ] It does **not** become a transfer. Detaching restores NULL; it never repoints an order at a
  different customer in one step. (Transfers are TKT-9/TKT-160 and have a different adversary.)
- [ ] `TestNoProductionCodeUpdatesOrderAttribution`'s allowlist grows to **exactly two** statements,
  and `TestTheAllowlistCannotBeWidened` covers the new one. That invariant is the thing keeping
  attribution honest; widening it is part of the work, not a side effect.
- [ ] The plan says whether an un-claimed order should be re-claimable by the same attacker
  immediately, and if not, what stops it.
- [ ] `make check` green.

**Non-goals:** transfers between accounts (TKT-9/TKT-160) · rate limiting the claim (TKT-224) ·
fixing the reference leak (TKT-202).

objective.note: A wrongly-claimed order can be detached, so 'someone else claimed my order' stops being a support request with no answer.

scope.note: Detach only — restore NULL. Never repoint at another customer in one step; that is a transfer (TKT-9/TKT-160) with a different adversary.

uncertainties.note: One genuinely open: whether an un-claimed order needs protecting from immediate re-claim by the same actor. Detaching restores it to the exact state the attacker claimed it from, so 'undo' without more is a loop. Options the plan must weigh: accept it (the operator can repeat), a cooldown, or a short-lived reservation for the rightful buyer. Deferred rather than open because it does not block starting and the ADR-021 framing is already written down.

dependencies.note: TKT-223 is Done - it creates the state this undoes. TKT-202 (references leak into gateway logs) is the CAUSE and is neither a blocker nor a substitute: this is recovery, that is prevention.

approach.note: Narrowed during shaping: a commerce /internal/ operation, reached by the back office with COMMERCE_STAFF_WRITE_TOKEN - the precedent is TKT-194's staff refund, which is the same shape (a support action on somebody else's order, guarded by an inline check per ADR-043, edge-denied at the gateway by construction). Authorization by role is ADR-042/TKT-197's matrix; the plan says which roles, and `finance` is probably not one of them.

first_slice.note: Detach + its audit record + the invariant amendment. The back-office surface can follow, or the first slice can be the internal operation alone if the plan argues it is demonstrable.

success.note: Deterministic: an attributed order becomes unattributed, the rightful buyer can then claim it, the action leaves a record, and TestTheAllowlistCannotBeWidened covers the SECOND allowlisted statement.

context_memo.note: Baked at creation; re-resolved 2026-08-06 when the ticket was shaped.

binding.rule: Local gate: `make check` (lint + test + build, Go & TS, plus the gateway smoke suite). CI runs the same gate - keep them mirrored. Commit regenerated code before running the gate.

governingAdrs.why: The TKT-223 amendment states the gap this closes, in the words this ticket quotes. Its 'one exception to attribution never changes' section is the rule the un-claim becomes a SECOND exception to - read why the first one was allowed before adding another.
Staff identity and the back-office session; TKT-197's role matrix is what would decide who may un-claim, if the back office is where this lands.
Declared `security:` guards public contract operations; an inline X-Internal-Token check guards the internal surface. This is an internal support action, so that rule decides its guard.
Name the adversary. An audit record inside the same database it audits constrains a careless operator, not a hostile one.
Do not add an order status. Attribution is its own dimension.

reference.summary: The statement to mirror and the guard to widen: `claimGuestOrderStatement` in services/commerce/internal/store/customer.go, allowlisted BY TEXT AND BY COUNT in attribution_invariant_test.go. Exactly one is permitted today; this ticket makes it two, and TestTheAllowlistCannotBeWidened must cover the second.

PREREQUISITE, not a coincidence: TKT-202 (the gateway logs guest_order_ref via the URL path). ADR-049 calls it a safety issue for claiming rather than logging hygiene - a leaked reference is what makes a hostile claim possible in the first place.

<!-- sdlc:stage=backlog kind=summary -->
Filed by TKT-223 (ai-review stage, gateless run 2026-08-06). Not shaped: `readiness` is mostly `open` and it must go through `shaping.md` before Gate 1. The three open questions are who may un-claim, what is recorded, and whether an un-claimed order needs protection from immediate re-claim by the same actor.

<!-- sdlc:stage=backlog kind=readiness -->
### Implementation readiness — CONCERNS

Shaped 2026-08-06, after TKT-21 closed. Gate 1 granted by the owner in the same instruction.

| Criterion | Status | Note |
|---|---|---|
| Objective | OK | "Someone else claimed my order" gets an answer |
| Scope | OK | Detach only — never a transfer |
| Uncertainties | WARN | Re-claim protection, deferred to the plan |
| Dependencies | OK | TKT-223 Done; TKT-202 is the cause, not a blocker |
| Approach | OK | **Narrowed during shaping** — see below |
| AC verifiable | OK | Including the allowlist growing to exactly two |
| Context-mémo | OK | Re-resolved today |

**What shaping decided:** a commerce `/internal/` operation reached by the back office with
`COMMERCE_STAFF_WRITE_TOKEN`. The precedent is **TKT-194's staff refund** — the same shape exactly: a
support action on somebody else's order, guarded by an inline check (ADR-043), edge-denied at the
gateway by construction, and driven from a back office that already holds that credential and has a
role matrix (ADR-042/TKT-197). This is not a new pattern; it is an existing one applied again.

**Concerns:**

1. **Undo without more is a loop.** Detaching restores the order to precisely the state the attacker
   claimed it from, so they can claim it again a second later. The plan must decide between accepting
   that, a cooldown, or a short-lived reservation for the rightful buyer — and each has a different
   adversary story (ADR-021).
2. **The audit record's adversary needs naming.** A row in the same database the operator can write
   constrains a *careless* operator, not a hostile one. ADR-021 is explicit that state inside the
   database cannot constrain someone who writes to the database — say which is meant before writing
   "audited".
3. **TKT-202 is the cause and is still open.** This ticket is recovery; that one is prevention.
   Shipping only this leaves the leak; shipping only that leaves today's wrongly-claimed orders stuck.
   They are complementary and neither substitutes.

**Verdict:** CONCERNS — proceedable. The mechanism is decided from precedent; what is left is one
genuine product question and one honesty question about the audit claim.

<!-- sdlc:stage=ready kind=claim -->
### Claim — TKT-225

**⚠ GATELESS RUN — all four human gates waived by the repo owner**, same terms as TKT-198 and
TKT-229, extended to this ticket by the owner's instruction on 2026-08-08 ("now do tkt-225"). Gate 1
was granted at shaping; Gate 2 self-resolved after the cross-model critique, preferring the
critique's recommendation and otherwise the most reversible option; Gate 3 agent-merged after the
adversarial review converges; Gate 4 self-validated against test evidence on merged code.

**Blocker verified clear:** the `blocked-by TKT-223` link is satisfied — TKT-223 is **Done**. The
status is priority, not feasibility, so this was checked rather than assumed.

**Selection reason.** The owner asked for it, and it is the only remaining shaped `Ready` ticket. It
also closes a real gap: ADR-049 § TKT-223 states in its own words that a claim is *"destructive,
exclusive, permanent and unrecoverable… The buyer's recourse is nothing."* Today the only remedy is
a manual `UPDATE` against the commerce database.

**Risk verdict: `risk:low` NOT claimed.** Explicitly refused — it fails three carve-outs:
- **auth** — the operation needs a guard decision (ADR-043), and the back office's staff credential
  is currently accepted by *exactly one* internal route, enumerated by a test;
- **data migrations** — an audit record almost certainly means a new table and migration 0019;
- **>5 files** likely, across store, api, migrations, the OpenAPI contract and the invariant test.

More to the point: this ticket **deliberately widens a security invariant**
(`TestNoProductionCodeUpdatesOrderAttribution` allows exactly one attribution write today, and this
makes it two). Widening a guard is the last thing that should ride a low-risk label, and on a
gateless run there is no human downstream to catch it.

**Governing ADRs, re-resolved at claim time** (the mémo is a 2026-08-06 snapshot):
- **ADR-049** — creates the gap, in the words the ticket quotes. Its "attribution never changes,
  with one exception" section is the rule this becomes a **second** exception to.
- **ADR-043** — decides where the guard lives: `security:` for public contract operations, inline
  token checks for `/internal/`.
- **ADR-042** + TKT-197's role matrix — who may do this, if the back office is the surface.
- **ADR-021** — **name the adversary.** An audit row inside the database it audits constrains a
  careless operator, not a hostile one. Any "recorded" claim must say which.
- **ADR-016** — do not add an order status; attribution is its own dimension.
- **ADR-051 — NEW since shaping (TKT-224, merged 2026-08-07), and worth checking.** It rate-limits
  `/orders/claim` per subject and per source. It does not obviously govern an internal un-claim, but
  the *interaction* matters for one of this ticket's own ACs: "should an un-claimed order be
  re-claimable by the same attacker immediately?" The limiter is now part of that answer and did not
  exist when the question was written. Flagged for the plan.

**Two constraints found in the code before planning, so the plan does not rediscover them:**
1. `claimGuestOrderStatement` (`store/customer.go:451`) is allowlisted **by text and by count** —
   `allowedAttributionUpdates` matches the exact normalized string `customer_id = $2`, and
   `TestNoProductionCodeUpdatesOrderAttribution` asserts `allowed == 1`. A detach sets
   `customer_id = NULL`, which that function will **refuse**. Both must change, deliberately.
2. `staff_credential_test.go` enumerates the internal routes and asserts the staff credential is
   refused by all of them **except** the refund (`staffOrInternal`, `refunds.go:69`). Making the
   un-claim staff-reachable means updating that enumeration — which is the test's whole point.

**Branch:** `TKT-225-unclaim-guest-order` off `origin/main` at `a0a596d`.

<!-- sdlc:stage=planning kind=plan -->
### Plan draft — drafted by `gpt-5.6-luna` (config.models.plan)

Run via the codex companion, `task --model gpt-5.6-luna --effort high --background`, READ-ONLY (no
`--write`). The drafter read the real tree. Clean run: no foreign-skill hijack, no "No job found"
false negative.

---

## 1. Decision

Build `POST /internal/orders/{id}/unclaim`, guarded by existing `staffOrInternal`, with a back-office action on `/admin/orders` for `admin` and `box_office`. Commerce will lock the completed attributed order, set `customer_id = NULL`, and insert an audit/block record in one transaction. The detached customer cannot immediately reclaim that order; a different customer can. This is an attribution recovery action, not a transfer, status change, lifecycle event, or reference-leak fix.

A. Recommend `staffOrInternal`. This preserves the existing internal-token operator path while making the action usable by support staff through the existing `X-Commerce-Staff-Write-Token`. The back office derives `actor` from the authenticated staff session; the form cannot supply it. `staff_credential_test.go` must be updated so exactly refund and unclaim accept the staff credential; every other internal route remains 404. Internal-token-only would be simpler but would leave support agents without a supported back-office workflow and would not provide individually identified staff actions.

B. Add a commerce-owned `order_attribution_detachments` table containing order ID, detached customer ID, actor, reason, and timestamp. The audit insert and attribution update commit together. This provides accountability against careless operators or application omissions, not tamper evidence against a commerce-database writer. The access lifecycle chain is rejected because it belongs to another service/domain and would not protect commerce database state.

C. Permanently block the detached customer ID from reclaiming that order. ADR-051 rate limiting only slows an attacker and does not prevent immediate reclaim within the remaining budget. A cooldown would also block the legitimate buyer. The block allows another customer to claim the restored guest order, while attacks using another account remain outside this ticket’s guarantee.

D. Extend the attribution scanner with exactly two statement-bound cases: normalized `customer_id = $2` with claim predicates, and normalized `customer_id = NULL` with detach predicates (`id = $1`, completed status, and non-NULL attribution). `scanAttributionUpdates` remains the complete match/recognize/authorize decision. The production count becomes exactly two, and `TestTheAllowlistCannotBeWidened` drives synthetic source through the scanner to reject a third statement or weakened predicates.

## 2. Definition of Done

- AC1: An operator can detach a completed attributed order; `customer_id` becomes NULL and another customer can claim it.
- AC2: Authentication uses `staffOrInternal`; the back office permits only existing `admin` and `box_office` roles, while finance remains denied.
- AC3: Every successful detach records actor, reason, previous customer, order, and timestamp atomically.
- AC4: The action only clears attribution; it never assigns another customer or changes order status, money, tickets, or `updated_at`.
- AC5: The source invariant allows exactly two attribution-update statements, and rejects a third or widened statement.
- AC6: The detached customer is blocked from immediately reclaiming; a different customer remains eligible.
- AC7: Generated code is committed before `make check`; `make check` passes. `make browser` submits the back-office form and verifies the resulting database state.

## 3. Files to change

- `docs/adr/ADR-052-order-attribution-detachment.md` — NEW; record guard, audit threat model, permanent reclaim block, atomicity, and non-goals.
- `docs/development.md` — document operator procedure, required reason/actor, refusal behavior, and audit guarantee boundaries.
- `services/commerce/api/openapi.yaml` — add unclaim operation and request/response schemas.
- `services/commerce/internal/api/openapi_gen.go` — GENERATED; regenerate and commit.
- `services/commerce/internal/api/server.go` — register `/internal/orders/{id}/unclaim`.
- `services/commerce/internal/api/staff_credential.go` — update comments for two staff-reachable operations.
- `services/commerce/internal/api/staff_credential_test.go` — enumerate unclaim as the second staff-credential exception.
- `services/commerce/internal/api/unclaim.go` — NEW; authentication, validation, store call, and response mapping.
- `services/commerce/internal/api/unclaim_test.go` — NEW; auth, validation, success, and refusal tests.
- `services/commerce/internal/store/customer.go` — add detached-customer block predicate to guest claiming.
- `services/commerce/internal/store/unclaim.go` — NEW; row-locking transaction, conditional NULL update, and audit insert.
- `services/commerce/internal/store/migrations/0019_order_attribution_detachments.sql` — NEW; audit/block table, constraints, index, and safe down migration.
- `services/commerce/internal/store/attribution_invariant_test.go` — widen scanner/count from one to exactly two statements.
- `services/commerce/internal/store/claim_smoke_test.go` — prove detached-customer refusal and different-customer reclaim.
- `services/commerce/internal/store/attribution_smoke_test.go` — prove atomic detach, audit contents, preserved timestamps/status, and rollback.
- `services/commerce/internal/store/migration_smoke_test.go` — verify migration schema and rollback refusal.
- `services/commerce/cmd/commerce/main.go` — update credential-scope comments.
- `services/commerce/cmd/commerce/credentials_test.go` — update credential-scope comments.
- `web/backoffice/src/lib/commerce.ts` — add direct commerce `unclaimOrder`.
- `web/backoffice/src/lib/order-console.ts` — parse nullable attribution and unclaim reason.
- `web/backoffice/src/pages/orders.astro` — add the authenticated unclaim form/action.
- `web/backoffice/test/api.test.ts` — test URL, credential, body, response, and failure mapping.
- `web/backoffice/test/order-console.test.ts` — test parsing and negative fixtures.
- `compose.yaml` — update staff-credential comments.
- `scripts/stack-env.sh` — update credential-scope comments.
- `scripts/browser.sh` — provision/pass a temporary box-office staff account for browser tests.
- `test/browser/unclaim-order.mjs` — NEW; submit the real back-office form and verify database/audit results.

`web/backoffice/src/lib/authorization.ts` and its existing tests require no route change because `/admin/orders` already admits `admin` and `box_office` and refuses `finance`.

## 4. Test plan

1. `TestNoProductionCodeUpdatesOrderAttribution`  
   RED once the new detach SQL exists but the scanner still allows only one statement. GREEN with exactly two allowed statements.

2. `TestTheAllowlistCannotBeWidened`  
   RED because the detach statement is initially refused. GREEN when both approved statements pass through `scanAttributionUpdates`, while a third assignment and weakened predicates remain refused.

3. `TestPredicatesAreReadFromTheStatementAndNotTheFile`  
   RED if the new implementation checks predicates at file scope. GREEN when claim and detach predicates are checked against their own statements.

4. Attribution smoke tests  
   RED before migration/store implementation. GREEN when a locked completed attributed order becomes NULL, exactly one audit row is written, and status/`updated_at` remain unchanged.

5. Atomicity/concurrency smoke test  
   RED before transactional implementation. GREEN when a failed audit insert rolls back the attribution update and concurrent claim/detach operations serialize without losing audit evidence.

6. Claim smoke tests  
   RED because the detached customer can currently reclaim. GREEN when that customer receives `ErrOrderNotClaimable`, while another customer can claim the restored order.

7. Migration smoke tests  
   RED because migration `0019` and its table do not exist. GREEN when constraints/indexes are present and rollback refuses while evidence exists.

8. `unclaim_test.go`  
   RED because no route/handler exists. GREEN when missing or wrong credentials return 404, valid staff/internal credentials pass, malformed inputs return 400, and store errors do not leak detail.

9. `staff_credential_test.go`  
   RED because the real router gains an unaccounted route and the old “refund only” assumption fails. GREEN when only refund and unclaim accept the staff credential.

10. Back-office unit tests  
    RED because no client/parser/form exists. GREEN when the exact direct request is sent, actor comes from the session, target-customer fields are ignored/refused, and NULL responses are validated.

11. `test/browser/unclaim-order.mjs` via `make browser`  
    RED because the form submission path does not exist or leaves attribution intact. GREEN only after real Chrome signs in, submits lookup and unclaim, and the database shows NULL attribution plus one audit record.

12. `make generate` followed by `make check`  
    RED on generated-code drift or any Go/TypeScript/lint/build/smoke failure. GREEN after generated output is committed and the out-of-band migration job applies `0019`.

No test can prove tamper evidence against a hostile commerce-database writer; that guarantee is explicitly not claimed.

## 5. Risks

- The shared staff credential authenticates the back office as a deputy, not an individual. Session-derived actor attribution can still be forged by someone holding the bearer credential.
- The permanent customer/order block can hinder recovery if support detaches the wrong customer. Undoing that block is outside this ticket.
- ADR-051 does not stop reclaim through another account, source rotation, replica restart, or direct service access.
- Audit rows are ordinary commerce state and can be altered or deleted by a database writer.
- Claim and detach must be reviewed together: both need completed-order predicates, detach must require non-NULL attribution, and claim must reject only the detached customer while preserving eligibility for others.
- The update, audit insert, claim block, generated contract, back-office client, and Astro form can each be correct while composing incorrectly; the smoke, unit, generated-code, and browser gates must all pass.
- This does not implement transfers, cooldowns, rate-limit changes, gateway log redaction, lifecycle-chain integration, or database-adversary tamper evidence.
